convoLines.text: I don't want to be in charge. I want us to survive. Those look the same from the outside.
"Cliffhanger — It goes perfectly still. It hunts at night — give the dark a wide berth."
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
Ruby won't meet your eyes. "I told myself finders keepers. It wasn't finders keepers. I'm sorry."
"Someone asked me yesterday what the plan was. I had one. That's new. That's — something."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on wanting to be in charge."
They glance away, then back. Different subject, same worry:
"Finally. I was wondering when you'd see my value."
"A name. Okay." You say it out loud, trying the shape of it:
"Roles. Not ranks — promises."
"Anyway — that's my cross to carry. What's on your mind?"
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"This was good." They mean it.
"When's the last time you really laughed?"
"Stealing joy. I like that. We should steal more of it."
"Three days ago. Someone dropped a whole basket of tubers and we just stood there laughing. It wasn't even funny. It was the standing there."
"Look — Still on the last time you laughed."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Vito is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
You show them Dandelion — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"I greet everyone by name each morning. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
"I should go. You know where to find me."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"What's your first memory? Like, ever. The earliest thing. ...anyway, where was I."
"Three. That's young. The brain keeps what it needs, I guess."
"Mine's Columbus, Ohio, I think — heat on pavement, someone's hand huge around mine. Or I invented it. First memories are half real and half the story you needed. Not that it matters."
"Still on your first memory."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Since Vito died... I keep expecting to see Vito at the fire. Stupid."
You show them Dandelion — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"I keep turning over the last thing Vito said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"Anyway — I should get going."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Hey — I found some Dandelion today. You were right, it was right where you said."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on that plant lesson."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
You show them Pokeweed — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Never mind the food I needed — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."

"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Vito always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
The ease drains out of it, a little.

"Sleep's gone strange. I write everything down at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"The fire feels smaller without Vito. The rest of us will have to be bigger."
"Still on what's been happening."

"Right. Go on, then."

"We never did finish talking about what's been happening — that was 11 days back. Still on your mind? 'You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.'"
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
"I buried this before the Scattering. Seemed stupid to keep it secret." Maricela digs up a wrapped bundle — food, still good. (+1085 kcal to the pantry.)
"We lost the illusion that the treeline holds itself. That's a kind of progress."
"Someone has to show the new folks where the door IS. That's me now, I guess."

"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."

"As I said — Still on what's been happening."

"About how this changed you — Has this changed you? Like, fundamentally? ...at least, that's how it looks to me."
"The old you got you here. The new you keeps you here. Both count."
The warmth pulls back a notch. They're weighing something.
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on how this changed you."
"I work alone. Nothing personal. ...It's a little personal."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
"I'm not from Denver. I'm from Shanghai, China. I was embarrassed. Everyone here was someone, and I was... that."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
